summary: Cartographers is a light roll-and-write style flip-and-write game where players simultaneously draw shapes onto their own map to satisfy the queen's shifting seasonal demands while blocking encroaching monster tiles. It's quick, low-stress, and works surprisingly well solo or at large table counts.
praised: quick, satisfying puzzle with simultaneous play so no downtime
great replayability from varied edict decks and seasons
works well solo and scales easily to big groups
criticised: luck of the shape draw can swing scores
some feel it lacks depth for repeated heavy play

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with shared shape reveals
interaction.detail: Everyone draws the same revealed shape onto their own individual map each turn, so the only shared element is the shape and scoring conditions being revealed, while each player's grid stays completely private. There's essentially no direct player-to-player action beyond racing to fulfill the same public objectives better than others.

subsystems: seasonal edict scoring (drawing terrain shapes to match active scoring cards)
sources: coin bonuses from placed ruin/coin tiles
monster tile penalty for empty squares
scoring.how_you_win: You win by drawing the offered shapes onto your map to best satisfy the four active seasonal scoring cards, ending with the highest total reputation after the fourth season.
